name: 4-speed compound
note: Four distinct speeds, and the only shape that fits on beams. A shifted stage can only be framed if its gears sum to a multiple of 16, and of those sums only 32 offers more than one shiftable ratio -- 8+24, 12+20 and 16+16. So both stages sit two studs apart, and they have to pick DIFFERENT pairs from those three: two identical stages give four combinations but only three distinct speeds, which is what gearbox-3-speed-compound.json is. Stage one takes 8+24 and 16+16, stage two 12+20 and 16+16, giving 0.200, 0.333, 0.600 and 1.000. The 8+24 is what makes it possible and it needs the early hardware: 2471 is the one 24-tooth clutch gear and 2473a the one ring that grips it.
